t: You're looking at Hurlingham House, in the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham. It was commissioned by John Ellis, who owned it and who is recorded as its builder. He lived from 1757 to 1832 and was a Fellow of the Royal Society. Later on, the banker John Horsley Palmer died in the house in 1858. Palmer was Governor of the Bank of England from 1830 to 1833. So the house links a builder of the late eighteenth and early nineteenth century with one of the leading figures of the Bank of England.
